result.summary: Allows running -txindex concurrently with block pruning as long as the index contains no legacy file-offset entries. When a transaction lookup targets a block that has been pruned from disk, txindex and GetTransaction return the candidate block hashes so RPC and REST callers can distinguish missing transactions from pruned ones. Callers can then retrieve missing blocks on demand using getblockfrompeer and retry.
result.problem: Running -txindex has historically been incompatible with -prune because index entries stored direct file positions on disk. Pruned node operators were unable to maintain a transaction index to locate historical transactions or provide input data for RPCs like getrawtransaction and utxoupdatepsbt without keeping the entire blockchain on disk.
evidence: Resolves four long-standing issues requesting txindex support on pruned nodes: #10609 (opened in 2017), #12651, #16182, and #35240
Enabled by #35531 (merged), which migrated txindex entries to store block hashes and packed block positions instead of disk file offsets
result.scope_notes: Changes the node::GetTransaction signature to return a TxLookupResult variant (TxFound or TxMiss), touching txindex, REST, and multiple RPC endpoints (getrawtransaction, gettxoutproof, and PSBT processing).
result.changed_since_previous: Includes release notes, handles missing undo data in getrawtransaction verbosity 2, and skips unavailable transactions when updating PSBTs.
result.card: Allows Bitcoin Core nodes to run txindex concurrently with block pruning when the index contains no legacy file-offset entries. When a transaction lookup targets a pruned block, GetTransaction, REST, and RPC calls (getrawtransaction, gettxoutproof) surface candidate block hashes in structured error data so callers can fetch the block via getblockfrompeer and retry. It addresses several issues opened since 2017 requesting txindex support on pruned nodes (#10609, #12651, #16182, #35240), building on the index key format changes merged in #35531.

risk.why: A bug in transaction availability checks or error reporting could break RPC lookups or cause utxoupdatepsbt to mishandle unpruned versus pruned inputs.
